radiology_report:
Subject: Prostate Multiparametric MRI | Facility: Spaarne Gasthuis, Haarlem | Date: 08 Jan 2025
Clinical indication: Assessment of a PSA level reaching 5.2 ng/mL alongside a previously positive biopsy result.
FINDINGS: Glandular volume registers at 47.0 mL. T2-weighted sequences delineate a distinct, hypointense focus within the right mid peripheral zone, spanning 12 x 9 mm. Diffusion-weighted and ADC maps reveal pronounced restriction, while DCE imaging captures rapid, robust contrast uptake. Capsular integrity remains intact, with no seminal vesicle involvement. Pelvic nodal basins appear normal.
IMPRESSION: PI-RADS 5 lesion identified in the right mid peripheral zone. PSA density stands at 0.11. Predicted csPCa probability is 0.8199149

previous_notes.author: Dr. E. Mulder (GP)
previous_notes.text: Initial evaluation took place in July 2023 after a routine screening flagged an incidental PSA level of 2.3 ng/mL. A subsequent transrectal ultrasound-guided sampling confirmed low-grade adenocarcinoma (Gleason 3+3). He was subsequently directed to the urology service. The current re-referral follows a PSA climb to 5.2 ng/mL and fresh multiparametric MRI results, warranting specialist reassessment.
